SourceTerm: 一氣不言含有象，萬靈何處謝無私
CreatedBy: Codex Iriya construction lane C evidence-first

Senses.PreferredTarget: one breath speaks no words yet contains all forms, while the myriad beings have nowhere outside its impartiality from which to give thanks
AlternateTargets: without speaking, one breath contains every form; no being stands outside its impartial reach
one vital breath is wordless but form-bearing, impartial to every being
SearchAliases: where can all beings give thanks
Senses.Note: Four distinct answer and comment deployments span four independent works.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且正令當行，如何理論？乃擊拂子曰：一氣不言含有象，萬靈何處謝無私。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 34–120). Jinshan Zhong strikes the whisk and gives the couplet after asking how the active command is to be stated.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且功不浪施一句作麼生道？一氣不言含有象，萬靈何處謝無私？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB388.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yikui of Shending. Yikui Yuankui gives the couplet as his answer to the request for a sentence in which effort is not spent in vain.

Occurrences.Kwic: 法林音云：東禪恁麼道，還扶得起國師麼？南堂欲云：國師不得雲門，洎合勞而無功；總似雪竇，未免白日見鬼。如今或有人問，但向道：一氣不言含有象，萬靈何處謝無私？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1297.xml). Tradition Mirror Grove. Jialing Xingyin reviews earlier comments on the national teacher and supplies the couplet as the answer he would give a questioner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 正與麼時，且知恩報恩一句作麼生道？一氣不言含有象，萬靈何處謝無私。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1414.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liao’an Qingyu. Liao'an Qingyu gives the couplet as the answer to his own request for a sentence that knows and repays beneficence.

Senses.Explanation: One breath says nothing yet contains visible forms; the myriad beings have nowhere outside its impartial reach from which to offer thanks. Chan masters preserve the two lines as one answer about an active command, effective work, and repaying beneficence. Jinshan strikes the whisk before giving it; Yikui gives it for a sentence in which effort is not wasted; Jialing offers it after reviewing earlier case comments; and Liao'an gives it for knowing and repaying beneficence.
